rv.q: Impeccably choreographed, beautifully staged and exquisitely sung, this Motown fable is one jukebox musical that'
And with a soundtrack of the Temptations’ greatest hits, many of them stitched into our pop culture, it’s hard not to have a good time.
This one is a hugely superior example of the genre.
Rarely has a show of its kind felt more like a jukebox musical by numbers.
Here’s one that is a couple of hours of unalloyed pleasure, and that deserves to be a great big fat popular hit.
So, that admirable attempt to add more heft to a jukebox show is only a partial success.
...this is a production that doesn’t fit its venue, lets its audience down by failing to trust them on the tough stuff and takes the easier staging option too frequently.
Ain’t Too Proud is a show where you are never more than a moment away from your next big smile.
If you like the music of The Temptations, you’re going to love Ain’t Too Proud, hit after hit are performed by the talented cast, from ‘My Girl’ to ‘A Rollin’ Stone’.
Each performer brought an unmatched degree of brilliance, honesty, and charisma to their parts, and the performances of all the characters were nothing short of extraordinary.

cn.t: Critics find this Temptations jukebox musical mostly delivers slick entertainment through dynamite performances and impeccable choreography, though some dismiss it as formulaic cruise-ship fare that doesn't reinvent the genre.
